title: metrics-and-logs-ingestion-sla-and-backfill-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for private (VPC / on-prem) observability ingestion focused on meeting tiered SLAs, performing safe retention/retention-policy upgrades, and executing a controlled backfill for missing historical metrics/logs after collector or pipeline changes. Goal is to provide runbook-level steps developers, SREs, and customer-facing engineers can follow when upgrading collectors, changing remote_write endpoints, or increasing retention in a customer-managed environment.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to customer VPC and on-prem deployments using: Prometheus (remote_write to long-term TS store), Grafana for dashboards (Grafana Agent or direct), OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel) for logs and traces, and Kafka/S3 as intermediate log storage options.
- Assumes Terraform-managed infra modules are in use for: prometheus, grafana, otel-collector, log-forwarder, and s3-archive.
- Bandwidth/ingest budget constraints are common in on-prem: include safe throttles.
- This is intentionally pragmatic: partial automation, clear manual check points.

High-level upgrade / change workflow (recommended):
1) Design & impact analysis (pre-change)
   - Identify the change: collector config, remote_write URL, retention period, scrape interval, or new metric labels.
   - Run a cost/ingest estimate using the workload profiler (link in linked_artifacts). Estimate delta in samples/sec and storage/day.
   - Map dashboards/alerts that will be affected (search Grafana for panels referencing metrics).
   - Create a Jira ticket with roll-forward and rollback criteria (include example queries and thresholds).

2) Helm/Terraform dry-run and staging validation
   - Run terraform plan and helm diff for modules: otel-collector, prometheus, grafana-agent.
   - Apply to staging VPC first. Validate metrics arrive, timestamps are correct, and no label explosions.
   - Confirm Prometheus scrape targets count matches expectation.
   - Smoke test dashboards: 3 representative dashboards (infra, inference-latency, request-cost) must render without errors.

3) Canary in prod (0 -> small -> large)
   - Start with 1-2 hosts or a small subset of traffic. Enable new remote_write or updated collector config for canary slice using feature-flagged Terraform variables.
   - Monitor ingestion rate, queue length on collectors, CPU/memory on grafana-agent, and SLO metrics (ingest_success_ratio, write_latency_p95).
   - Run log sampling checks: ensure structured fields (env, model_id, request_id) are present.

4) Ramp and finalize
   - Gradually increase to 25%, 50%, 100% over controlled windows (prefer low-traffic times).
   - Validate alerting silence and dashboard integrity at each step.
   - Once at 100% for 24–48h with no regressions, mark the Jira ticket as ready to finalize.

Backfill strategy (when metrics/logs are missing due to previous drop):
- Use case: collector misconfiguration or pipeline interruption caused gaps for 6–72h. Customers often require backfill for billing / QA.
- Approach: avoid re-scraping with full load; instead rehydrate from buffered storage or traces/log archives.
  1) Confirm source buffer: check if otel-collector or agent had local disk buffer or Kafka backlog. If backlog exists, throttle re-ingest via collector limits.
  2) If samples are not buffered but application stores metrics (pushgateway, sidecar), coordinate an application-side replay: expose a restricted replay endpoint.
  3) For logs: if logs archived to S3 or on-prem object store, run a controlled reprocessing job that re-emits logs into log-forwarder and tag them with a backfill marker (backfill=true, backfill_window). This avoids confusing alerting (alerts should ignore backfill-tagged data).
  4) Timing and QoS: schedule backfill at off-peak windows. Cap ingestion to a percentage of peak (default: 25% of peak tokens/sec) to avoid destabilizing downstream long-term store.

Terraform module notes (practical snippets and gotchas):
- prometheus module:
  - Keep remote_write blocks configurable and templated; avoid inlining endpoints. Use map(var.remote_write_endpoints).
  - Expose scrape_interval and scrape_timeout as variables with safe minimums (15s / 10s) for customer infra with constrained control plane.
  - Add a flag for federation vs direct remote_write to LT store. Federation can massively reduce cardinality (recommended for very high cardinality workloads).

- otel-collector module:
  - Provide two deployment patterns: agent (daemonset) + gateway (centralized). Make batching and queue_size configurable.
  - Default queue_size small in on-prem (5000 items) and provide a liquidity_policy variable for overflow (drop_oldest vs block).
  - Enable default processors: attributes (drop), resourcedetection, batch, and memory_limiter.

- log-forwarder module:
  - Use topic-per-tenant pattern in Kafka; terraform should template topic configs with retention.ms and max.message.bytes aligned with customer limits.
  - Provide an s3-archive module with lifecycle policies and index manifests for backfill jobs.

Testing matrix / acceptance criteria:
- Functionality tests:
  - Prometheus -> remote_write latency p95 < 2s for samples under normal load.
  - No dropped series more than 0.01% in 24h.
  - Grafana dashboards render panels (no "no data" or NaN spikes unrelated to incident).

- Load tests:
  - Run 1-hour soak at 1.2x expected peak ingestion; ensure collector CPU < 85% and disk buffers do not exceed 60% capacity.
  - Run a dedicated backfill rehearsal in staging with 1TB archived logs reprocessed; measure throughput and impact on downstream queries.

- Safety & rollback conditions (stop upgrade and rollback if any met):
  - sustained increase in write_latency_p95 > 3x baseline for 15+ minutes.
  - queue_length on gateway > 80% for 10 minutes.
  - Alert noise: number of firing alerts doubles compared to baseline and does not self-resolve in 30 minutes.

Operational runbook snippets (quick actions):
- If collectors fall behind:
  - Temporarily reduce scrape_interval to 60s for non-critical targets via terraform var and scale down endpoints in central gateway.
  - Increase collector batch_max_size to allow larger write batches.

- If downstream remote_write fails:
  - Flip an emergency flag in remote_write config to fallback endpoint (we maintain a read-only cheaper LT store for emergency ingest).
  - Notify on-call and schedule immediate mitigation: reduce ingest by 50% and enable sample downsampling.

Alerting & dashboard recommendations:
- Alerts: ingest_success_ratio < 99.5% for >5m, collector_queue_fill > 75% for >10m, remote_write_error_rate > 0.5% at p95.
- Dashboards: create a top-level "Ingest Health" board with rows: collector health, agent resource utilization, queue lengths, remote_write latency, and backfill progress.
- Tagging: all backfill/replay traffic MUST be tagged with backfill=true and backfill_window to ensure alert rules suppress or downgrade their severity.

Migration considerations for retention increase:
- Plan cost delta estimates; customers must accept the storage delta or opt for tiered retention (hot/warm/cold).
- For Prometheus: consider thinning (rollup) older samples (e.g., 1m -> 5m) instead of full retention at same resolution. Provide a Terraform switch to enable rollups using a batch job that compacts TS with tooling in long-term store.

Open questions / TODOs (editable checklist):
- [ ] Decide policy for label cardinality limits per tenant (default: 2000 series/target).
- [ ] Add a Terraform module param to enable backfill-marker injection automatically during reprocessing jobs.
- [ ] Document S3 manifest format used by reprocessing tooling.
- [ ] Standardize Grafana provisioning for backfill-aware dashboards (hide panels when backfill=true).

Appendix: quick command cheatsheet
- Check collector queue: kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector | grep queue_size
- Check prometheus series count: curl -sS localhost:9090/api/v1/series?match[]=up | jq length
- Force a canary terraform apply (example): terraform apply -var 'canary_hosts=["host-42"]' -target=module.otel-agent

Notes & provenance:
- Drafted during the on-prem observability sync (2026-02). Reviewed with Tom and Sofia for backfill strategy. Intentionally leaves room for local infra limitations — please update customer-specific runbooks with exact thresholds and contact points.
